title: F4: four-entry recovered collimation with fixed quarter qubitization

claims.statement: For every integer N>=2 and every fixed s in Z/NZ, F4 is the single fixed-four-entry, quarter-qubitization, critical-profile square-root-base algorithm in proof.md Sections 1-7, with n=ceil(log2 N) and L=log2 n. For n>=256 its maximum width B is the first sequential trial with retained capacity at least n, U=ceil(sqrt(B)), f(b) is the least f>=4 with 2f-floor(f/4)>=b+ceil(log2(b+1))+6, and its decrement is ceil(log2((f(b)+1)^2)). Every base costs two supplier leaves. For 1<=n<256 it uses the specified exhaustive branch. From independent ideal source copies it returns the entire secret with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3. Total charged sequential work is O(n^(11/4) L^(13/4) 2^((177/250)sqrt(nL))). For n>=256 the stronger executed-profile bound is O(n B^(7/2) log2(B+2)^(-1/2) log2(n+2)^2 2^(B/2)). It charges source acquisition, extraction precision, classical bit operations, addressing, circuit generation, all four simultaneous endpoints and cleanup, decoding and every failed attempt. The growth index of the supported envelope is 0.5. All four resource bounds hold jointly on every execution branch, including incorrect labels, wrong earlier estimates, retries and aborts. The representatives are positive for n>=2. Every 1<=n<256, including n=1 where L=0, uses the finite branch. Constants are absolute, independent of N, s and outcomes.

For n>=256 total source acquisitions on every branch obey Q<=ceil(1024*(2 Emax*(nK+2n)+2n)), where Emax is the exact all-D rational maximum in proof.md Section 5, initialized at TWO leaves, and K is fixed in Section 7. For 1<=n<256, Q<=N(n+10). This counts every rejected, discarded, failed and retried copy. Uniformly Q=O(n^(7/4) L^(3/4) 2^((177/250)sqrt(nL)-(59/100)(nL)^(1/4))). For n>=256 the stronger cap is O(n B^(3/2) 2^((B-U)/2)). The growth index of the supported envelope is 0.5. Every base costs two supplier leaves. For 1<=n<256 it uses the specified exhaustive branch. From independent ideal source copies it returns the entire secret with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3. For every n>=1 the guaranteed malformed fraction is epsilon(n)=0. At most floor(0*Q)=0 acquired copies may be malformed, so every copy is an independent ideal coset state. Under precisely this model the same unconditional success and all four every-branch resource bounds hold jointly. No impossibility of positive tolerance is claimed.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
